prompt: SNES-era 16-bit pixel art inspired concept rendering of a wide side-scrolling arcade shooter stage backdrop, bold dark outlines, saturated limited palette, crisp pixel-art texture accents, subtle CRT scanline glow, a lifted deep-navy base that is never pure black. A violent night storm over a high mountain range, seen side-on as layered horizontal bands that overlap with no empty gaps. The upper third is a low, heavy ceiling of churning storm clouds in slate blue and cold lilac grey stretching across the whole width, with a ragged break near the top left where a strip of cold navy sky and a few faint stars show through. Below it, a long serrated chain of tall snow-covered mountain peaks rises straight out of the clouds across the full width, sharp saw-tooth silhouettes of pale ice-blue rock with hard white windward faces lit from the left and deep navy lee shadows, long thin plumes of blown snow streaming sideways off every summit. From the cloud ceiling, one jagged branching bolt of violet lightning strikes down onto a central peak, its lilac glow lighting the cloud undersides around it. The lower third is a roiling sea of storm cloud that swallows the feet of the mountains, flat stacked slabs of slate blue and lilac grey with heavy dark outlines, their tops torn into horizontal wind streaks. A curtain of slanting rain falls across the entire scene on one consistent diagonal, thin pale needles. Palette of storm blues, lilac greys, ice whites and one violent violet accent. No characters, no aircraft, no text, no letters, no user interface.
